state.case_summary:
A 52-year-old South Asian man presented with a 3-month history of a gradually enlarging swelling of the left cheek. On examination, there was a diffuse, firm, non-tender mass measuring about 4 × 5 cm that extended from the infraorbital region superiorly to the lip commissure inferiorly, medially obliterating the nasal ala, and laterally approaching the preauricular area. Intraoral examination revealed a well-defined vestibular swelling measuring 4 × 3 cm, extending from the distal aspect of the left canine to the second molar. Routine hematologic parameters were within normal limits. Contrast-enhanced CT of the head and neck showed a mildly homogeneously enhancing soft-tissue density lesion in the left premaxillary region with adjacent bony destruction of the maxillary alveolus. Based on the clinical findings, a provisional diagnosis of malignancy of the left maxilla was made, and the differential diagnosis included benign tumor, sarcoma, lymphoma, and melanoma. An incisional biopsy suggested myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia.

Options:

C. Malignancy of the left maxilla was initially considered
D. Benign tumor was included in the differential because of the soft
E. Sarcoma was considered due to the bony destruction seen on CT
F. Lymphoma was entertained given the firm facial swelling and imaging features
G. Melanoma was part of the imaging
H. Inflammatory pseudotumor was suspected intraoperatively on frozen section
